test_title: PYST 26: Selection Post (Graduate Level) - GA (Held On 29 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct options:
Assertion (A): Jeremy Bujakowski was the first Indian to compete at the Winter Olympics, participating in the 1964 and 1968 Games.
Reason (R): India did not participate in the Winter Olympics for 20 years after Bujakowski's era.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A.**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Assertion (A)** states that **Jeremy Bujakowski** was the first Indian to compete at the **Winter Olympics**, participating in the **1964** and **1968 Games**. This statement is **correct**. **Jeremy Bujakowski**, an alpine skier, made his debut at the **1964 Winter Olympics** in **Innsbruck, Austria**, where he was the sole representative for India. He returned to compete in the **1968 Winter Olympics** held in **Grenoble, France**.

• **Reason (R)** mentions that **India** did not participate in the **Winter Olympics** for **20 years** after **Bujakowski's era**. This statement is also **correct**. Following the **1968 Games**, India did not send any athletes to the Winter Games in **1972 (Sapporo)**, **1976 (Innsbruck)**, **1980 (Lake Placid)**, and **1984 (Sarajevo)**. India only returned to the competition at the **1988 Calgary Games**, marking a exactly **20-year hiatus**.

• While both statements are factually accurate, the **Reason (R)** describes a period of absence that occurred **after** the events mentioned in the **Assertion (A)**. The lack of participation for **20 years** does not provide a causal explanation or logical reason as to why **Jeremy Bujakowski** was the first participant or why he competed in those specific years. **Hence, R is not the correct explanation of A.**

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Jeremy Bujakowski** was of **Polish descent** but represented **India** after his family settled there. In the **1964 Innsbruck Games**, he competed in the **Men's Downhill** event but was unable to finish due to an injury. In **1968**, he competed in **Downhill**, **Slalom**, and **Giant Slalom**, achieving his best finish of **53rd** in the **Downhill** category.

• The **1988 Calgary Winter Olympics** marked India's return to the global stage with a three-member contingent. **Shailaja Kumar** became the **first Indian woman** to compete in the **Winter Olympics** during this edition, participating in **Alpine Skiing** alongside **Gul Dev** and **Kishor Rahtna Rai**.

• **Shiva Keshavan** is perhaps the most famous Indian Winter Olympian, having represented the country in **six consecutive Winter Olympics** from **1998 (Nagano)** to **2018 (Pyeongchang)**. He competed in the **Luge** event and holds the record for being the **youngest person** to ever qualify for the Olympics in Luge at the **age of 16**.

• The **Winter Olympics** are held every **four years** and include sports such as **Skiing**, **Ice Hockey**, **Figure Skating**, and **Luge**. The first-ever **Winter Olympic Games** were held in **1924** in **Chamonix, France**.

• In recent years, India's participation has remained small but consistent. At the **2022 Beijing Winter Olympics**, **Arif Khan** was the only Indian athlete to qualify, competing in both **Slalom** and **Giant Slalom** events.

**Important Points__**

• **First Indian Winter Olympian:** **Jeremy Bujakowski** (**1964**).

• **First Indian Female Winter Olympian:** **Shailaja Kumar** (**1988**).

• **Longest Gap in Participation:** **20 years** (**1968 to 1988**).

• **Most Appearances:** **Shiva Keshavan** with **6 appearances**.

• **Governing Body:** The **Indian Olympic Association (IOA)** manages India's representation, while the **Winter Games Federation of India** oversees the development of winter sports in the country, primarily centered in regions like **Gulmarg** and **Auli**.
